acceptance.given: A package declares a secret-using capability without naming a runtime credential owner.

oracle.expected: The validator reports a validation failure identifying the missing runtime credential owner and applicable A15 rule, without exposing credential values or unrelated secret content.
forbidden: Validation succeeds despite the missing runtime credential owner.
The diagnostic includes a credential value or raw secret content.
oracle.observable: A pytest case invokes the real validator entry with a disposable package missing the credential-owner field and inspects the structured result and rendered diagnostics for failure status, A15 rule/location, and secret-free output.

acceptance.then: Validation fails with a structured diagnostic for the missing runtime credential owner and no credential value disclosure.
acceptance.when: During validation of the package, the validator evaluates the secret-using capability declaration and its runtime credential-owner field.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reject secret-using capability declarations that omit a runtime credential owner while emitting only location and rule diagnostics without secret values.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted schema or state change; rollback restores prior validator behavior and preserves package declaration compatibility.

slice_hint.state_transition: A package with a missing runtime credential owner transitions from inspection input to a failed validation result with an A15 diagnostic.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted A15 pytest node and the complete capability-test module pass against the real validator entry, exercising the structured failure and redaction assertions.
